title: Жидкая курица и группа захвата  (Liquid Chicken and the Arrest Team)

segments.t: Back at Claude Monet, Katya serves her signature molecular dish—liquid chicken spread across the plate. After devouring several portions, the young police lieutenant tells his captain that his heart is beating faster and he craves another plate, convincing the captain to summon a tactical arrest squad.
Подождите, это что, настоящая жидкая курица?
Тихо, они её специально так тонко размазали.
Дорогие гости, пробуйте наше новое горячее блюдо!
Ну, скажи честно, что ты сейчас чувствуешь?
Кажется, моё сердце бьётся намного быстрее!
И мне очень хочется ещё такой еды!
Прямо не могу остановиться, как вкусно!
Всё понятно, это точно сильный стимулятор!
Они подмешивают порошок прямо в курицу!
Товарищ капитан, что мы теперь будем делать?
Немедленно вызываем сюда нашу группу захвата!
А сейчас мы покажем вам наш десерт!
Let's examine how the detectives talk themselves into calling a police raid.
Подождите, это что, настоящая жидкая курица?
'Wait, is this real liquid chicken?' The guest anchors one key term toward the inspector: "nastoyashchaya" means "real, genuine" (from "nastoyashchiy"), giving the line its exact edge.
Тихо, они её специально так тонко размазали.
'Quiet, they spread it out so thinly on purpose.' The inspector follows up steadily in this moment, grounding the moment in plain reality.
Дорогие гости, пробуйте наше новое горячее блюдо!
'Dear guests, taste our new hot dish!' Katya holds firm right away with a sigh, bringing things back to earth after the buildup.
Ну, скажи честно, что ты сейчас чувствуешь?
'Well, tell me honestly, what do you feel right now?' The inspector grounds one practical expression at once: "chuvstvuyesh" means "feel" (from "chuvstvovat"), giving the line its exact edge.
Кажется, моё сердце бьётся намного быстрее!

'It seems my heart is beating much faster!' The guest gives this statement to the inspector: the "-sya" ending on "kazhetsya" ("it seems, I think") turns the action inward or makes it happen between people naturally.
И мне очень хочется ещё такой еды!
'And I really want more of this food!' The guest continues warmly during the talk, steering the talk right where he wants it.
Прямо не могу остановиться, как вкусно!
'I literally cannot stop, it is so tasty!' The guest emphasizes this vivid term at once: "ostanovitsya" means "to stop", and it carries the main weight of what the guest is saying.
Всё понятно, это точно сильный стимулятор!

'Everything is clear, this is definitely a strong stimulant!' The inspector phrases this update beside Katya: notice how Russian needs no word for "am", "is", or "are" in the present — placing the words side by side says it all.
Они подмешивают порошок прямо в курицу!
'They are mixing the powder right into the chicken!' The inspector speaks warmly with a smile, watching the guest's face to see how the news lands.
Товарищ капитан, что мы теперь будем делать?
'Comrade Captain, what are we going to do now?' The guest emphasizes this telling expression in earnest: "tovarishch" means "comrade", and it carries the main weight of what the guest is saying.
Немедленно вызываем сюда нашу группу захвата!
'We are immediately calling our arrest team here!' The inspector fires back evenly across the room, letting the remark speak for itself.
А сейчас мы покажем вам наш десерт!

'And now we will show you our dessert!' Katya continues sharply to settle things, keeping the focus on what actually matters here. Now let's hear the complete liquid chicken scene again at full speed.

Mistaking their own excitement and appetite for synthetic narcotics, the detectives radio for backup. Next, Chef Barinov has to escape another crisis at Lyova's apartment. See you next time!
